title: The forenoon prayer
hook: a voluntary prayer when the sun is up

segments.voice: Yesterday, tahajjud, the night prayer, and your line: awake for him. If you woke in the night, what did you give that first minute to? Now the sun comes up. Day one thousand eighty-three.

"By the morning hours." That's how Pickthall opens surah ninety-three, and the Arabic word behind those morning hours is today's word. Duha is not dawn. Dawn already has its prayer, fajr, prayed in the gray before sunrise. Duha comes later: the sun is fully up, the commute has happened, the first coffee is gone, the inbox has started to fill. The middle of the morning, the stretch that is easiest to stop noticing. Islam puts a prayer there too. Nobody is required to pray it. Today, the prayer for the hour when the day is already busy.
screen: `BY THE MORNING HOURS.` → `NOT DAWN: LATER.` → `WHEN THE DAY IS ALREADY BUSY.`

segments.voice: Duha is a voluntary prayer, prayed after the sun has risen well into the sky and before the heat of noon. Its smallest form is two units. First, the hour itself has a surah. Surah ninety-three swears by the morning hours and by the stillness of the night, and then tells the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that his Lord has not left him. A report in Sahih al-Bukhari ties it to a time when he had fallen ill and missed his night prayers, and someone taunted him that he had been abandoned. So the forenoon, in that surah, is a sign of being remembered. Second, a hadith in Sahih Muslim gives the prayer a surprising job. Every morning, it says, a charity is owed for each joint of your body. Every glorifying of God is a charity, every word of praise, every good deed urged and every wrong discouraged. And then: two units prayed in the forenoon are enough for all of it. Your knuckles, your knees, your jaw, the small hinges you never think about. Two units cover the thanks. Third, a witness. Umm Hani reported that on the day Mecca was opened, he bathed in her house and then prayed eight units in the forenoon, lighter than any prayer she had seen from him, yet with full bowing and prostration. Two units are enough; that morning she saw eight. Fourth, the timing has a picture. Another report in Sahih Muslim calls it the prayer of those who often turn back to God, and says its time is when the young camels feel the heat of the sand. Not a clock time. A moment you'd notice if you were outside. Scholars give the window in hours and minutes now, but the hadith gives it in hot sand.
screen: `THE HOUR HAS A SURAH.` · `A CHARITY FOR EVERY JOINT.` · `UMM HANI SAW EIGHT.` · `WHEN YOUNG CAMELS FEEL THE HEAT.`

segments.voice: The practice is two units mid-morning. For now, settle where you are. Slowly open and close your hands. Feel each knuckle bend. Roll your shoulders, turn your neck a little, flex your feet. Each joint is one of the charities the hadith counts. If you pray, you can plan two units of duha for later this morning, or pray them now if the sun is up. If you don't, let each joint you move be one thank-you, said without words. The bell holds the time.
Duha. The forenoon, when the sun is well up, and the voluntary prayer prayed in it. Today's word.
Your line: the forenoon prayer. Today, somewhere between breakfast and lunch, stop for two minutes: two units if you pray, two minutes of stillness if you don't. Day one thousand eighty-three.

howItsDone: Muslims who keep the duha prayer pray at least two voluntary units after the sun has risen well and before the time of the noon prayer, often at work, at home, or in the mosque after a morning class.

original.note: Arabic: the forenoon, when the sun is well up. surah 93, ad-Duha, takes its name from it.

trapdoor: what you thought: a morning prayer, like the one at dawn.
what it means: a voluntary prayer after the sun is well up, two units at least.
what a scholar hears: the hadith of the joints in Sahih Muslim, and a timing given not in hours but in the moment young camels feel the hot sand.
recall: the wash that reaches the whole body

notes: Editor: cut Abu Hurayrah's three counsels (Bukhari 1981/1178), which day 1081's hook had just used, and replaced them with Umm Hani's forenoon report (Bukhari 1176: eight units on the day Mecca was opened, light but with full bowing and prostration); confirm number and wording. The occasion of surah 93 is restated closer to Bukhari 4950 (illness, missed night prayers, a taunt of abandonment) instead of 'revelation had paused and people mocked him'. The older note's mention of Bukhari 1981 no longer applies.
Pickthall 93:1 quoted from memory as 'By the morning hours'; confirm.
Bukhari 4950 cited for the occasion of surah 93 (a pause in revelation and mockery); confirm the number and that the link is fairly stated.

Muslim 720 (charity on every joint; two rak'ahs of duha suffice) paraphrased; Bukhari 1981 (Abu Hurayrah's three counsels) paraphrased; the counts 'three days' and 'three things' come from that hadith.
Muslim 748 (salat al-awwabin when the young camels feel the heat) is stated as being about duha; confirm the identification is acceptable across schools.
'Its smallest form is two units' and the window 'after the sun has risen well ... before noon' reflect common fiqh; confirm. Larger numbers of units (e.g. Umm Hani's report) deliberately left out.
